body.x: PIA Space Inc. participated in CES 2024, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th (Tuesday) to 12th (Friday, local time).

Established in 2021, PIA Space is an AI technology-based company currently developing and commercializing a solution that utilizes multi-modal artificial intelligence (AI) to detect specific situations in CCTV. Particularly, the company is commercializing the MACS (Multi-modal AI for CCTV Situation detection) technology, which can detect complex conditions that conventional intelligent CCTV systems may not properly identify. PIA Space is conducting Proof of Concept (PoC) for various potential clients in Korea and Singapore.

Participating in CES 2024, PIA Space showcased its main product, the CCTV Real-time Video Automatic Monitoring Solution (MACS). MACS is a real-time video automatic monitoring solution applicable to security CCTV, CCTV safety monitoring, and CCTV security solutions. It automatically detects complex situations, securing the golden time to reduce critical damage by triggering alarms and subsequent actions. Notably, this solution can detect difficult-to-analyze violent or criminal cases and recognize risks such as falls from various heights by contextualizing hazardous situations.

PIA Space is conducting pilot projects with domestic institutions, including the Gwangjin-gu and Songpa-gu Office, to test its AI-based CCTV solution, MACS. On the international front, PIA Space is engaged in Proof of Concept (PoC) projects with KABAM Robotics, supplying security robots at Singapore Changi Airport and Semb Corporation, a plant operator on Jurong Island. Plans include expanding paid services within the CCTV control rooms of various district offices in Korea and supplying automated surveillance solutions to Singapore Changi Airport, large hotels, and more. PIA Space aims to achieve approximately $12 million in revenue by 2025, targeting markets including North America.

PIA Space stated, "At this exhibition, many government officials and corporate security personnel from North America, South America, and Turkey visited our booth. Visitors were in a situation where they did not know how to utilize their existing CCTV systems effectively. However, they responded positively, expressing that our product could enhance the utility of their CCTV systems," adding, "We want to create user cases that verify whether we can accurately align our technology with the needs of potential clients and implement the desired services for them."

body.x: Furthermore, they stated, "While we are a startup driving technology development and commercialization domestically, our target market is the entire global CCTV solution industry. Through our participation in CES 2024, we aim to create partnership opportunities with leading CCTV operators in the North American market. We aspire to become a leading AI-based CCTV solution provider in the North American market and beyond."

CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is held in Las Vegas every January, providing a comprehensive view of global technology industry trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies and conducting ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ selections. Additionally, through ‘AVING LIVE,’ they provide live coverage of CES issues.

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion operated on the most historical scale since Seoul’s first participation in CES in 2020, with the largest exhibition area, number of participating companies, and supporter numbers. Seoul Metropolitan Government collaborated with 13 institutions to design The Seoul Pavilion, which is essential in Seoul’s endeavors to establish Seoul as a startup hub. Among the participating companies in the Seoul Pavilion, 17 received innovation awards, proving their capabilities. Collaborated institutions include Seoul Business Agency, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul Campus Town, Yangjae Innovation Hub, Gwanak-gu, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, and Kyunghee University, totaling 13. Seoul City and institutions and supporters participating in industry-academic cooperation are matched 1:1 with companies, with a maximum of 85 supporters participating.
